upd.in_use:
MCP for Primavera P6 is in use by: {names}.

Close it in these programs now and update? They lose access to it until you restart them (a write in progress is cancelled). Or the update installs by itself as soon as they close.
upd.note: Updates and the skill shop are the only network requests MCP for Primavera P6 makes, both to GitHub. Updates: it asks GitHub for the latest release, then downloads the installer, checks its SHA256 against the release's SHA256SUMS.txt and installs it silently. Your MCP client settings are kept. Turn the option off to only check when you click Check now.
about.tagline: A local MCP server for Primavera P6 Professional databases and XER files.
about.privacy.text: MCP for Primavera P6 runs only on this PC and sends nothing anywhere: it only reads GitHub for the optional update check and the skill shop (when you open it or ask for it; sharing a skill is done by you on GitHub). But the data its tools return goes to the AI model your MCP client uses, which may be a cloud service. For confidential schedules, use a local model.

ins.intro: Instructions are sent to the AI by every MCP client when it connects to MCP for Primavera P6. They apply to every conversation that uses the P6 tools.
ins.locked.tip: This rule protects the database: writes always need a dry run and your explicit yes.
ins.text: Instruction (one rule, written for the AI):
ins.custom.note: Example: When you show an activity, always write its Activity ID and name as Activity ID - Activity name (A1230 - Excavation), never the ID alone. Untick an instruction to keep it without sending it.
ins.restart: Click Save, then restart your MCP client (Claude Desktop, VS Code...) so that it reads the new instructions.
skill.intro: P6 skills are ready-made workflows that chain P6 tools (for example p6-weekly-update-review). Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and Cline read them from their skills folder and use one when your request matches its description (install them on the MCP clients page); clients that support MCP prompts, such as Claude Desktop, also list them as prompts.
skill.col.title: Title
skill.share.note: Share sends one of your skills to the MCP for Primavera P6 skill shop: the skill is copied to the clipboard and a GitHub form opens in your browser (a free GitHub account is needed): paste the skill and click Create. It is published once the maintainer approves it. Without an account, Export a zip file and send it: Import adds it here. The same zip can be uploaded as a skill in Claude Desktop.
skill.share.ask: Share the skill {name} publicly in the MCP for Primavera P6 skill shop ({repo})? MCP for Primavera P6 copies the skill to the clipboard and opens the GitHub form in your browser: sign in if asked (or create a free GitHub account), paste the skill in the Skill field (Ctrl+V), tick the license box and click Create. It is published under the Apache-2.0 license after the maintainer's review. Never share client names or project data.

remote.about: claude.ai and ChatGPT in the browser
remote.about.what: Remote access lets claude.ai and ChatGPT, in the browser or on a phone, use MCP for Primavera P6 on this PC. They reach it through your own Cloudflare account (free) and a tunnel this PC opens: no port is opened on your network. Each connection is approved here on this PC.
remote.about.privacy: What leaves the PC: the answers of the tools the AI app calls (activities, dates, float, checks), as with Claude Desktop, but through Cloudflare and the AI vendor's servers. The database and XER files are never uploaded. This PC must stay on with MCP for Primavera P6 running in the notification area.
